instruction.text: Select all the uses of a semi-colon.

trainers.hint: An adverbial is a word, phrase, or clause that describes how, when, where, why, or to what extent something happens in a sentence.

b: indicates the end of a sentence

instruction.text: Drag the semi-colon to the correct place in the text.

atoms.a: She enjoyed the beach; however, the scorching sun made her retreat to the shade.
atoms.b: She enjoyed the beach((++;)) however, the scorching sun made her retreat to the shade.

atoms.a: He couldn’t find his keys; they were hidden under the pile of newspapers on the table.
atoms.b: He couldn’t find his keys((++;)) they were hidden under the pile of newspapers on the table.

atoms.a: The concert was cancelled; consequently, many disappointed fans were left waiting outside the venue.
atoms.b: The concert was cancelled((++;)) consequently, many disappointed fans were left waiting outside the venue.

atoms.a: Sarah excels in mathematics; moreover, she’s passionate about science.
atoms.b: Sarah excels in mathematics((++;)) moreover, she’s passionate about science.

instruction.text: Drag the semi-colons to the correct places in the text.

atoms.a: Martin Luther King Jr: “Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate; only love can do that.”
atoms.b: Martin Luther King Jr: “Darkness cannot drive out darkness((++;)) only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate((++;)) only love can do that.”

atoms.a: My best friends are Tilly and Josh; they are both super cool and hilarious. I also have a friend called Amelia; I love how she always looks out for me.
atoms.b: My best friends are Tilly and Josh((;)) they are both super cool and hilarious. I also have a friend called Amelia((;)) I love how she always looks out for me.
